observations.seen: A single repeating corridor of flat boxes and planes in a void; no landmarks, no variation over 1.4 km.
Track is pure primitives. The vehicle is a kitbash of spheres and boxes with an odd "minus-sign" disc face that reads as a toy or robot face, not a craft.
No textures visible anywhere; every surface is a flat color or a gradient.
The vehicle has a glossy dark clearcoat with some specular highlights. Everything else is unlit emissive or basic transparent material.
Only the vehicle shows PBR response. The floor and walls show no roughness or metal variation, and the neon has no physically plausible energy.
No light from the neon falls on the floor, walls or vehicle. The vehicle is lit by a generic key and reads as a black hole.
No vehicle contact shadow and no obstacle shadows, so the vehicle floats with no ground anchoring.
Ambient is near zero; the vehicle's back faces crush to pure black.
The vehicle shows faint env reflections. The floor has a slight sheen near the walls but no real reflection of the neon, a huge miss for this genre.
Not blown out, but the neon is clamped flat with no HDR rolloff. Whites on the vehicle discs clip hard.
The palette is coherent (cyan/magenta/yellow/purple) and sRGB output looks correct. Saturated but controlled.
Edges on the arches and floor lines look acceptable at 1080p. Thin vertical lines likely shimmer in motion (inferred).
No bloom on a neon game, no vignette, no chromatic or speed effects. It looks like a raw forward pass.
No thruster flames, trails, speed lines, impact or pickup effects visible in any frame.
A few static dots in frame 2 only.
The vehicle pose is identical across frames except for a vertical translation for the jump. No bank, tilt or squash is visible.
The hero craft is oversized, nearly black against a dark scene, and its design has no clear read (face? wheels? engines?).
The chase cam sits too low and too close, so the vehicle occludes the play lane. Static FOV, no speed response.
Dead-center symmetric framing with the hero blocking the focal point; the vanishing point is hidden behind the vehicle.
Strong linear perspective from the arches and floor lines helps. No fog or atmospheric falloff, so depth reads as a flat diorama.
No fog, haze, sky, stars, grid horizon or volumetrics. A flat void.
Obstacles ahead are hidden behind the vehicle (frame 4's obstacle is nearly invisible), and pickups are small and low-contrast at the sides.
The desktop glass bar is clean and legible but generic web-dashboard styling. The Restart button in gameplay HUD and on-screen buttons on desktop feel like a debug layout.
A clean sans with good hierarchy (small caps labels, bold values), but generic and with no genre personality.
No feedback is visible: static style meter, "intro" section at 1.5 km, identical frames 1000 m apart.
The canvas is collapsed to a quarter of the screen, the HUD covers it, and 75% of the screen is blank. Not shippable.
Reads as an early prototype or programmer-art runner with a broken mobile layout.
